blocks.content: Chandigarh's demography chapter is compact but high-value — its extremely high literacy rate and unusually skewed urban population are two of the most frequently tested comparative facts across all Indian states/UTs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India accounted for approximately 17.5% of the total global population according to the 2011 Census.
Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate at 94.00%, whereas Bihar recorded the lowest at 61.80%.
Hindi is the most widely spoken language in India, followed by Bengali, Marathi, and Telugu.
The population density of India stands at 382 persons per square kilometer according to the 2011 Census.

cells: ≈ 818 females per 1,000 males — among the lowest (most skewed) of any Indian state/UT, reflecting heavy in-migration of male workers
≈ 86.4% — among the highest of all Indian states/UTs
≈ 97% — one of the highest urbanisation rates of any Indian state/UT (the UT is almost entirely a single city)
≈ 9,258 persons per sq km — among the highest in India, a direct consequence of its tiny area and large urban population
≈ 17.1%, driven mainly by in-migration rather than natural growth

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Chandigarh appears at BOTH extremes in national rankings depending on the metric: near-highest literacy AND near-highest population density, but among the LOWEST sex ratios — a combination worth memorising for 'which state/UT ranks highest/lowest in X' style questions.

items: Punjabi and Hindi are the two most widely spoken languages, reflecting Chandigarh's location straddling Punjab and Haryana and its large Punjabi-refugee-origin founding population; English is widely used in administration, education and business.

Sikhism and Hinduism are the two largest religious communities, with smaller populations of Muslims, Christians, Jains, Buddhists and others — broadly mirroring the religious composition of the wider Punjab-Haryana region from which most residents' families originally migrated.

A significant share of Chandigarh's founding population in the 1950s were Partition refugees from West Punjab (now in Pakistan), resettled here as the new capital was built — giving the city a strong intergenerational Partition-refugee heritage still referenced in its social and political life.

Panjab University, Chandigarh — a premier central university established in its present location in 1947 (originally founded in Lahore in 1882, relocated after Partition) — is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities associated with the erstwhile Punjab region.

The Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education & Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh — established in 1962 — is one of India's foremost public medical institutions and a major regional referral hospital for Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.

Chandigarh College of Architecture, Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH-32), and several central schools/institutions add to the UT's outsized concentration of higher-education and healthcare infrastructure relative to its tiny population.
Chandigarh consistently ranks near the top of India's Human Development Index-style comparisons among states/UTs, reflecting its high literacy, healthcare access, and per-capita income together.
Exams frequently contrast the overall sex ratio (940) with the declining child sex ratio (918 for 0-6 years).
Bihar has the highest population density among states (1,106 per sq km), while Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest (17 per sq km).
Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1,084 females per 1,000 males), whereas Haryana has the lowest (879 females per 1,000 males).

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Panjab University's Lahore origin (founded 1882, relocated after 1947 Partition) is a favourite 'which institution moved after Partition' style question, paired with PGIMER (1962) as Chandigarh's flagship medical institution.

items: Population ≈10.55 lakh (2011); sex ratio ≈818 (among India's lowest); literacy ≈86.4% (among India's highest).
≈97% urban population — one of the highest urbanisation rates of any Indian state/UT.
Population density ≈9,258/sq km — among the highest in India.
Punjabi and Hindi are the principal languages; Sikhism and Hinduism the two largest religious communities.
Panjab University (est. 1882, Lahore; relocated to Chandigarh after 1947) and PGIMER (est. 1962) are the UT's flagship education/health institutions.
